project.name: Hero: RimWorld Is Still the Gold Standard for Letting Players Break the Rules

data.label: Style
data.name: Noir Comic Book
data.description: Noir comic book illustration style. Heavy black ink lines, high contrast shading, cel-shaded shadows. Hand-drawn graphic novel aesthetic with bold outlines. Muted palette with selective color pops. Stylized, not photorealistic. No text, watermarks, speech bubbles, or white borders. Edge-to-edge composition filling the entire frame.

data.label: Action
data.content: Comic book hero image for an article about RimWorld as a modding and player-agency sandbox: a dark sci-fi colony workshop seen from above, tiny colonists moving between rough metal rooms, glowing storyteller control panels, tangled mod cables and rule cards being rearranged by player hands at the edge of the frame. Heavy ink linework influenced by Jack Kirby and Moebius, high contrast chiaroscuro, cel-shaded shadows, muted charcoal and rust palette with selective cyan and magenta UI accents, edge-to-edge composition, no text, no logos, no photorealism.

data.label: Avoid
data.content: Never include Lemmy Kilmister, Motörhead imagery, metal bassists in leather jackets, or self-portraits of rock legends. No generic punk rockers with mohawks unless specifically requested. Focus on the actual subject matter described in the scene.
